chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said:

I was selling the sabiriyya (fabric) in the shade, so Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) passed by me and said to me: 'O Hisham! Indeed, selling in the shade is cheating (ghishsh), and indeed, cheating is not permissible.'

key_terms.السَّابِرِيَّ: A type of fabric or cloth
key_terms.الظِّلَالِ: The shades (plural of shade, implying areas of shadow)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling goods in the shade in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of transparency in commercial transactions, where 'ghishsh' (deception) is defined by the concealment of defects due to limited visibility, such as selling in the shade. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ethical integrity in trade, linking physical concealment to moral dishonesty. The ruling underscores that valid consent requires full awareness of the commodity's quality, a key tenet in Islamic jurisprudence.
